Definition: from G1006; herbage (as if for grazing):--herb.
BiblicalUsage: Herb is the word for herbage, the green growth that feeds the flocks — and it appears once, in the picture of the fruitful earth. In Hebrews 6:7 the earth which drinketh in the rain that cometh oft upon it, and bringeth forth herbs meet for them by whom it is dressed, receiveth blessing from God. One word, for the ground that drinks the rain and bears fruit.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the herb in Hebrews is the test of the soil: the rain falls on all the ground, but only the ground that bears fruit receives the blessing.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
